correctness.rationale: For all L,v,D>0 the killed half-line diffusion has a first-passage mean L/v and a positive regenerative steady state. Differentiate the exact killed resolvent in Laplace time to obtain E[A|X=x]; the analytic identity 1+2g′(z)=2e^z(sinh z-z)/(e^z−1)^2 proves strict decrease below L and the formula gives derivative 1/v above L, hence a unique minimum. Five explicit Dirichlet potential polynomials verify E[X], E[A], E[AX] and Var(X), yielding the sharp Pe=√3 sign. The strong Markov property yields E[R|X]=X/v and the forward covariance. All claimed quantifiers, boundary limits and normalization are addressed. Direct numerical killed-kernel integrals for four triples and five conditioned x values and symbolic differential checks passed from packaged checker. Numerical tests are corroboration, not an infinite-domain proof.

value.rationale: Elapsed and remaining event times and instantaneous distance are natural observables in threshold-triggered diffusion and basic integrate-and-fire models. The result identifies a unique spatial minimum in conditional age, a sharp qualitative transition between diffusion- and drift-dominated age–position coupling, and a strictly positive time-direction difference that remains despite identical marginal age and residual distributions. The exact threshold and full-position classification are physically interpretable, not arbitrary finite slices or mere recomputation of known stationary moments. The theorem is model-specific and deliberately does not claim an entropy-production identity.
